steps.evidence: llm-cost cost --group-by task --days 30 (2026-11-09): rules review 24 calls, $0.699, mean $0.029 (median $0.0024, p90 $0.077), on earlier review models; the current review model (scripts/review_rules.py:18) has no registry price. 10 reviews per run follows the 10 unmatched attempts of the saved airfield run and falls as rulings become rules.

cost_basis.cheapest_design: The plain version, one judge call per unmatched attempt with no test run before install, would save the confirm call (about $0.02 per run), but the plain baseline showed it installs wrong or unusable rules (2 of 3 rejected by the rules check, 1 accepted with a wrong price). So the plan keeps the test run and one confirm call, calls the judge only for an attempt no rule covers, makes each ruling a rule so the same attempt never calls it again, and uses the interpreter's cheap model and route. Total about $0.34 per run with 10 rulings, most of it the existing rules review.

cases.finding: Today's built path recorded it as unmatched and changed nothing. The plain ruling named the factory's choice correctly, but its rule had no effects and was rejected by the rules check (participants must exactly name entity_ref fields).

plain_baseline.verdict: The plain version reads the world correctly at these sizes, so the judge's input starts from it (the whole world). It is not enough on its own: 2 of 3 rules were rejected by the rules check and 1 was accepted but wrong, so pass 2 (rules check and test run of the proposed rule before install, with one revision) is kept. Pass 1 (facts and nearby checks) showed no added value here and is kept only because it costs no call.

stage_effects.stage: pass 2: rules check and test run of the proposed rule before it is installed (J1, J3)
stage_effects.gap: the plain version's rules: 2 of 3 rejected by the rules check, 1 accepted with a wrong price; without this stage they would be installed or silently fail

stage_effects.stage: one revision after the test run (J2)
stage_effects.gap: a rejected or wrong rule from the first proposal (2 of 3 in the plain baseline) gets one more try before the attempt is refused as a language gap

stage_effects.stage: pass 1: facts the attempt touches and nearby rules' checks given to the judge (J1)
stage_effects.gap: on worlds too large to read whole, the judge could miss a blocker an installed rule already names; at today's sizes the plain version read the facts right, so the effect is not shown
